§ 2Content

§ 3SKELETAL SYSTEM — OVERVIEW

  • The skeletal system is the body's framework, providing support, protection, and allowing for movement. It comprises bones, cartilage, and ligaments.
  • Divided into the axial skeleton (80 bones) and the appendicular skeleton (126 bones).
  • Total: 206 bones in adults; 300 in children (bones fuse with age).

§ 4AXIAL SKELETON (80 bones)

The axial skeleton protects the brain, spinal cord, heart, and lungs; supports the head, neck, and body; and provides a rigid framework for muscle attachment.

Bones in Skull (22 total)

  • Cranial bones: 8
  • Facial bones: 14

Bones in Ear (6 total)

  • Incus, Malleus, Stapes (× 2 = 6).

Bones in Spinal Cord / Vertebral Column (26 in adults)

  • Cervical: 7 vertebrae (neck; C1 = Atlas, C2 = Axis)
  • Thoracic: 12 vertebrae
  • Lumbar: 5 vertebrae
  • Sacral: 5 vertebrae (fuse to form 1 sacrum)
  • Coccygeal: 4 vertebrae (fuse to form 1 coccyx / tailbone)

Bones in Rib Cage (24 + 1 = 25)

  • 24 ribs (12 pairs) + 1 sternum (central chest bone, connected to ribs via cartilage).

Hyoid Bone

  • A horseshoe-shaped bone in the neck, supports the tongue.

§ 5APPENDICULAR SKELETON (126 bones)

The appendicular skeleton provides support and leverage for limb movement; facilitates locomotion.

Shoulder Girdle (4)

  • Clavicle: 2
  • Scapula: 2

Pelvis (2)

  • 2 hip bones (each formed by fusion of ilium, ischium, pubis).

Arm (3 per side; 6 total)

  • Humerus, Radius, Ulna

Hand (27 per side; 54 total)

  • Phalanges: 14 (per side)
  • Metacarpals: 5 (per side)
  • Carpals: 8 (per side)
  • 14 + 5 + 8 = 27 per hand; × 2 = 54

Leg (4 per side; 8 total)

  • Femur (thigh): 1
  • Patella (kneecap): 1
  • Tibia: 1
  • Fibula: 1
  • 4 × 2 = 8

Foot (26 per side; 52 total)

  • Tarsals: 7
  • Metatarsals: 5
  • Phalanges: 14
  • 7 + 5 + 14 = 26 per foot; × 2 = 52

§ 6TOTAL BONE COUNT

  • Adults: 206 bones (80 axial + 126 appendicular).
  • Children: 300 bones (more, because some are not yet fused; they fuse with age).

§ 7Key concepts

  • Axial skeleton: 80 (skull 22 + ear 6 + spine 26 + ribs 25 + hyoid 1)
  • Appendicular skeleton: 126 (shoulder 4 + pelvis 2 + arms 6 + hands 54 + legs 8 + feet 52)
  • Total adults: 206; children: 300
